unit.why: A brief anecdote: R. Zusya covers himself in winter, is overcome by the awe of the angels, cannot bear it, and asks God to remove it.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a thematic anthology section 'מענין יראת שמים'. The next division holds a separate Zusya anecdote on the same theme.

stories.start_quote: וסיפר המעשה מרבי זוסיא שכסה עצמו
stories.summary_en: R. Zusya covered himself in winter and the awe felt by the angels came upon him; unable to bear it, he asked God to take the awe away from him.

quotes: ובא עליו יראת המלאכים ולא היה יכול לסבול אותה
tags.why: The story centres on an overwhelming religious awe.
The awe or dread is so intense he cannot bear it.
Apparently a winter self-mortification (rolling in or covering himself with snow?), but the wording is unclear.
He petitions God, though this is not formal liturgy.
The angelic awe descends on him supernaturally.
Angels are referenced through their awe; they do not act.
The tale is framed as being told by an unnamed speaker.
Embedded in a thematic teaching anthology on fear of Heaven.

missing_concepts: being overwhelmed by excessive spiritual experience and asking for its removal
angelic awe as a level of fear of God
